title: Author + implement PROP-NNN: add per-agent sparse-checkout (exclude monitor/integrity/ for agents that don't write there) + tighten stale-clone cleanup window from 24h to 4h + add startup pre-clean step to clone-using agents
background:
Repo's working tree on disk is currently ~574 MB. The vast majority is monitor/integrity/ which is in the process of draining from 892 stale source files down toward expected ~20-170 per retention policy (PROP-082 shipped 2026-06-07T06:08Z broke the prune↔workspace-sync re-add loop; natural drain estimated at 7-10 days). Even at post-drain steady-state (~100 MB working tree), every agent that clones the full repo pays the cost for the integrity directory it doesn't write to.

Agent classification by integrity-write surface:

  - **WRITES to monitor/integrity/**: integrity, prune-integrity, tinker (run reports), workspace-sync (skips log, run reports, audit files). These NEED the full directory.
  - **DOES NOT write to monitor/integrity/**: decider, analyst (Opus), analyst-baby, curmudgeon, curmudgeon-verify, dome-mirror, poller, social. These 8 agents could use sparse-checkout to exclude the integrity directory (or most of it) and reclaim per-clone headroom.

Reading-side nuance: decider's intake DOES read `monitor/integrity/report-*.json` (daily integrity reports) to triage Mech 2/3 findings. Sparse-checkout patterns must include the daily reports while excluding the per-cycle audit files (`narrative-cite-audit-*.json`, `verify-pending-run-*.json`, `workspace-sync-runs/`, `*-archive.jsonl`).

Additional headroom optimization: CLAUDE.md's per-session-clone-discipline section notes tinker's auto-cleanup catches clones older than 24h. Yesterday's empirical evidence showed a 208 MB `/tmp/tinker-clone` had survived from a crashed prior run for hours without being cleaned. Dropping the auto-cleanup window to 4h + adding a startup pre-clean step to each clone-using agent's prompt would catch same-session accumulation.

operator_decision.rationale: Both changes are additive prompt-edits with no functional risk. Sparse-checkout is well-understood git tooling. Cleanup window tightening is purely defensive. Combined estimated per-agent-clone savings: ~300-400 MB once the integrity dir drains; ~100-200 MB during the current bloat period.

requested_work: Step A1 — Per-agent audit: for each of the 8 sparse-eligible agents (decider, analyst, analyst-baby, curmudgeon, curmudgeon-verify, dome-mirror, poller, social), read its prompt file + reference docs and enumerate every path under monitor/integrity/ that the agent READS from (e.g. decider reads daily integrity reports, perhaps reads workspace-sync-runs sentinels for staleness checks). Document the read-surface per agent in PROP-NNN's evidence section.

Step A2 — Per-agent sparse-checkout pattern design: for each agent, design the include/exclude pattern. Operator pre-approves the following BROAD STROKES; tinker refines per-agent:
  - DEFAULT-INCLUDE for all 8: data/, monitor/decisions/, monitor/analyst/, monitor/curmudgeon/, monitor/scripts/, monitor/prompts/, monitor/tinker/, monitor/changes/, monitor/social/, monitor/sloppytoppy/, build*.js, test.js, build-scripts/, predictions/, docs/, CLAUDE.md, README.md
  - DEFAULT-EXCLUDE for all 8: monitor/integrity/narrative-cite-audit-*.json, monitor/integrity/verify-pending-run-*.json, monitor/integrity/workspace-sync-runs/, monitor/integrity/*-archive.jsonl, monitor/integrity/sync-workspace-runs-*.json, monitor/integrity/prune-integrity-runs/, monitor/integrity/git-to-fuse-divergence-*.json, monitor/integrity/dome-mirror-*.json
  - PER-AGENT-INCLUDE (decider only): monitor/integrity/report-*.json (the daily integrity reports decider needs for Mech 2/3 triage)
  If a Step A1 read-surface audit reveals an agent reads OTHER monitor/integrity/ paths not covered above, add to its per-agent-include list with a comment citing the read site.

Step A3 — Implement sparse-checkout in each agent's clone-setup. Pattern (operator pre-approved):
  ```bash
  git clone --depth 50 --filter=blob:none --no-checkout "${AUTH_URL}" "${CLONE}"  # SUSPECT: --filter=blob:none was explicitly disallowed by PROP-051 disaster lessons for some agents
  ```
  ACTUALLY — re-read CLAUDE.md PROP-051 safety gates A1-A4. Workspace-sync's safety gate A1 explicitly bans `--no-checkout` and `--filter=blob:none` for workspace-sync because the 2026-05-21 mass-delete incident traced to that path. **Workspace-sync stays full; agents in the sparse-eligible list need to verify their clone setup does not share safety-gate constraints.** For each of the 8 agents, check whether CLAUDE.md prohibits sparse-checkout / partial clone for that agent specifically. If any prohibition exists, EXCLUDE that agent from Part A and document the reason.
  Tinker designs the actual git incantation. Likely: `git clone --depth 50 --sparse "${AUTH_URL}" "${CLONE}"` followed by `git -C "${CLONE}" sparse-checkout init --cone` and a `sparse-checkout set <patterns>` block. Cone-mode is simpler and well-supported. Non-cone-mode allows fine-grained file-level patterns if needed for the monitor/integrity/report-*.json include.

Step A4 — Validate per-agent: simulate a sparse-clone of decider's clone-setup, count files materialized (`git ls-files | wc -l`), measure du -sh. Compare to current full-clone footprint. Document savings per agent in PROP-NNN.

Step B1 — Read tinker.md and find the auto-cleanup section that currently catches clones older than 24h. Replace `24h` with `4h` (or whatever shorter window tinker decides is safe — operator pre-approves anywhere from 2h to 6h).

Step B2 — Add a startup pre-clean step to each clone-using agent's prompt: at run start, before clone-create, scan `/tmp/*-clone` and `/sessions/*/dome-*-clone` directories. For each found clone-directory that is NOT the current agent's expected clone path AND has mtime older than 1h, `rm -rf` it. Idempotent + safe (only removes other-clone directories, not current run's).
Step B3 — Update CLAUDE.md per-session-clone-discipline section to reflect the tightened windows. Cite this directive + PROP-NNN.

Step 1 — Author monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-NNN-clone-headroom-sparse-checkout.json. Required sections: title, problem statement (cite this directive + the 574 MB / 7-day drain context + the 8 agents in scope), per-agent Step A1 read-surface table, per-agent Step A2 sparse-checkout pattern, Step B cleanup window changes, Q-OPs if any (especially: which of the 8 agents have CLAUDE.md prohibitions excluding them from sparse-checkout?), verification_pattern (grep + per-agent `git ls-files | wc -l` simulation), files_touched, estimated_loc.

Step 2 — Tinker self-applies per the recent pattern (PROP-076 through PROP-083) if total LOC <150 across the 8 prompt edits + tinker.md + CLAUDE.md + (any shared helper script). Hold for operator review if scope balloons or a Q-OP needs answering.

Step 3 — Per-agent post-deploy validation: tinker manually triggers each modified agent in a test-only mode (or schedules a single run) and verifies the sparse-clone setup works. If any agent fails to clone correctly, immediate rollback for that agent and operator-escalation.

Step 4 — Lifecycle: flip PROP-NNN.json status='implemented'. Flip this directive to status='completed' with prop_id_implemented set. Update CLAUDE.md's Two-Repo Architecture section if sparse-checkout changes any documented invariants.

Step 5 — Manually copy edited prompt files to FUSE so each agent's next session-bootstrap picks up the new clone-setup logic. dome-mirror will propagate within ~30 min but manual sync is the safe bootstrap path.
non_goals: Do NOT change workspace-sync's clone setup. PROP-051 safety gate A1 explicitly bans partial-clone shapes for workspace-sync. Stays full.
Do NOT change integrity, prune-integrity, or tinker's clone setup. They WRITE to monitor/integrity/ and need the full directory.
Do NOT change the prune-integrity script itself. Prune works correctly; only the rescue layer needed PROP-082's fix.
Do NOT attempt to migrate existing checkouts — tinker only modifies the clone-CREATION step. Existing clones will rebuild on their next agent-fresh-clone cycle.
Do NOT add `--filter=blob:none` to any agent. PROP-051 lesson: that flag was the disaster vector. Use `--sparse` checkout-config-style instead.
Do NOT scope to operator-side /tmp cleanup. Operator-session is a separate surface; this directive is for scheduled-agent sessions.
Do NOT touch sloppytoppy-* agents (currently disabled per 2026-05-21 mass-delete recovery). Stays as-is.

expected_output: (1) monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-NNN-clone-headroom-sparse-checkout.json with status='implemented'. (2) Edits to 8 agent prompts (decider.md, analyst.md, analyst-baby.md, curmudgeon.md, curmudgeon-verify.md, dome-mirror.md, poller.md, social.md or their relevant reference docs) installing sparse-checkout in the clone-setup step. (3) Edit to monitor/prompts/tinker.md tightening the auto-cleanup window from 24h to 4h. (4) Per-agent startup pre-clean step added. (5) Update to CLAUDE.md's per-session-clone-discipline section. (6) Per-agent validation simulation in PROP-NNN. (7) This directive at status='completed'. (8) FUSE-synced files.
estimated_effort: ~90-120 min Opus. Per-agent read-surface audit (Step A1, ~25 min). Sparse-checkout pattern design + implementation (Steps A2-A3, ~30 min). Cleanup window changes (Step B, ~15 min). Per-agent validation (~20 min). Lifecycle + FUSE sync (~10 min). The 8-agent scope is the longest step.
priority_note: MEDIUM — quality-of-life improvement, not blocking anything. The 7-10 day natural drain from PROP-082 addresses the immediate bloat; this directive prevents the post-drain steady-state from still carrying the cost of an unused directory. Worth shipping in the next 1-2 tinker runs but no rush.
